question: Walking at (3)/(4) of his normal speed from his home, Abhishek is 30 minutes late in reaching his office. The usual time taken by him to cover the distance between his home and his office is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Time ∝ 1/Speed ⇒ new time = 4/3 of normal time

Delay = (4/3 − 1) = 1/3 of normal time

1/3 of time = 30 minutes

Normal time = 30 × 3 = 90 minutes

**∴ Answer = 90 minutes**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

New speed = 3/4 of normal speed

Delay = 30 minutes

**Formula used:**

Time = Distance ÷ Speed ⇒ Time ∝ 1/Speed

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let normal time = t

⇒ New time = t × (4/3)

⇒ Delay = (4/3)t − t

⇒ Delay = t/3

⇒ t/3 = 30

⇒ t = 90 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 90 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Inverse Proportion

For fixed distance, time is inversely proportional to speed.

Speed Fraction Rule

If speed becomes a/b, time becomes b/a times.

Delay Concept

Extra time taken = New time − Original time.
